Detailed Event Description: Descending into Namrup, Sukaphaa establishes firm frontier peace through tactical deterrence and diplomatic accords with eastern Naga chieftains.

Event: First View of the Brahmaputra Valley
Detailed Event Description: Sukaphaa and scouts view the immense, fertile Brahmaputra River plain ('Mung Dun Sun Kham' - Country of Golden Gardens), recognizing its potential for wet-rice cultivation.

Event: Sukaphaa Enters the Assam Valley
Detailed Event Description: Formal arrival of Sukaphaa's royal entourage in the plains of Upper Assam along the Dihing river basin in 1228 CE, officially inaugurating the 600-year Ahom Dynasty.

Event: Establishment of the First Tai Settlements
Detailed Event Description: Initial settlements established at Tipam, Habung, and Shimolguri; stilt houses (Rwan-hon) constructed and virgin floodplains cleared for agriculture.

Event: The Sacred Promontory of Charaideo
Detailed Event Description: The sacred royal compound and ancestral temples at Charaideo, the spiritual center and eternal resting place of Ahom royalty.

Event: Institution of the Supreme Offices of Burhagohain and Borgohain
Detailed Event Description: Sukaphaa institutes the Great Council of Nobles: Thaomung Klinglunmang (Burhagohain) and Thaomung Kangngan (Borgohain), forming a hereditary prime-ministerial council.
Key Historical Figures: Chaolung Sukaphaa, First Burhagohain, First Borgohain

Event: Matrimonial Alliances with Borahi and Moran Rulers
Detailed Event Description: Sukaphaa adopts an assimilative policy by establishing matrimonial bonds with the indigenous Moran chief Bodousa and the Borahi king Thakumtha, marrying local princesses and integrating them into court governance.
Key Historical Figures: Chaolung Sukaphaa, Moran Chief Bodousa, Borahi King Thakumtha

Event: Introduction of Advanced Wet-Rice Cultivation (Sali Kheti)
Detailed Event Description: Introduction of advanced Tai hydraulic techniques, dyke bunding, canal irrigation, and deep-water transplanted Sali rice, producing an agricultural surplus.
Key Historical Figures: Chaolung Sukaphaa, Tai farmers and paiks

Event: Founding and Construction of the Sacred Capital at Charaideo
Detailed Event Description: In 1253 CE, Sukaphaa establishes the permanent royal capital at Charaideo (Che-Rai-Doi), consecrated with sacred Tai Phuralong rituals and ancestral invocations.
Key Historical Figures: Chaolung Sukaphaa, Deodhai and Bailung high priests

Event: Writing of the First Ahom Buranji (Royal Chronicles)
Detailed Event Description: Sukaphaa decrees that royal scribes and priests record every event, battle, decree, and genealogy on Sanchi bark (agarwood paper), establishing Assam's Buranji tradition.
Key Historical Figures: Chaolung Sukaphaa, Royal Tai scribes (Likhakar Barua), Deodhais

Event: The Royal Court of Sukaphaa
Detailed Event Description: Convening of the sovereign assembly at Charaideo; state administration organized with local leaders integrated, establishing a harmonious multi-ethnic polity.
Key Historical Figures: Chaolung Sukaphaa, Burhagohain, Borgohain, tribal ministers

Event: Institution of Royal Moidams (Pyramidal Earth Tumuli)
Detailed Event Description: Upon Sukaphaa's demise in 1268 CE, the tradition of building subterranean vaulted brick/stone chambers covered by hemispherical earthen mounds (Moidams) begins at Charaideo.
Key Historical Figures: Chaolung Sukaphaa, Royal embalmers, High priests

Event: Accession and Court Assembly of Suteuphaa
Detailed Event Description: Sukaphaa's eldest son assumes the golden throne and addresses the council of ministers to set aggressive policies for western border expansion.

Event: Frontier Standoff on the Dikhou River
Detailed Event Description: Ahom expanding settlements encounter the Kachari Kingdom's eastern outpost along the Dikhou River.

Event: Skirmishes on the Ahom-Kachari Frontier
Detailed Event Description: Military clashes between Ahom warriors and Kachari troops over control of fertile grazing and cultivation tracts along the Dikhou.

Event: Diplomatic Negotiations with the Kachari King
Detailed Event Description: Suteuphaa sends envoys to avoid destructive protracted war, initiating bilateral talks with the Kachari monarch.
Key Historical Figures: King Suteuphaa, Kachari King, Diplomatic envoys

Event: Demarcation of the Dikhou River Boundary
Detailed Event Description: Formal treaty demarcating the Dikhou River as the permanent mutual frontier between the Ahoms and Kacharis.

Event: Conspiracy of the Eastern Naga Clans
Detailed Event Description: Highland Naga chieftains withhold promised tributes and plot coordinated raids on Ahom valley villages.

Event: Suteuphaa Marshals the Royal Army
Detailed Event Description: King Suteuphaa mobilizes an expeditionary army equipped with iron-tipped arrows, daos, and war shields into the foothills.

Event: The Fierce Battle of the Naga Hills
Detailed Event Description: Ahom forces fight intense uphill engagements against fortified Naga hill positions, defeating hostile warriors in dense jungle terrain.

Event: The Fierce Battle of the Naga Hills
Detailed Event Description: Ahom forces fight intense uphill engagements against fortified Naga hill positions, defeating hostile warriors in dense jungle terrain.

Event: Naga Submission and Tribute Offering
Detailed Event Description: Defeated Naga chiefs travel to the royal court at Charaideo to kneel, submit oaths of loyalty, and pay tribute in salt, iron, and cloths.

Event: Consolidation of the Dikhou Frontier
Detailed Event Description: Peaceful agrarian settlements flourish across the pacified Dikhou frontier, securing Upper Assam's borders.

Event: Administrative Division of the Realm
Detailed Event Description: Subinphaa formally partitions administrative jurisdiction and subjects into two equal domains under the Burhagohain and Borgohain.

Event: Dual Provincial Governance by Gohains
Detailed Event Description: Burhagohain administers the northern/eastern territory while Borgohain administers the southern/western territory with autonomous judicial authority.

Event: Large-scale Swamp Reclamation and Bunding
Detailed Event Description: Large-scale drainage canals, dykes, and earthen bunds constructed across alluvial marshlands to open vast new paddy fields.

Event: Outbreak of the First Ahom-Kamata War
Detailed Event Description: King Sukhangphaa leads an offensive against Raja Durlabhanarayana of Kamata, seeking westward expansion into Lower Assam.

Event: Frontier Battle with Kamata Forces
Detailed Event Description: A pitched riverine engagement between Ahom war flotillas and Kamata defensive troops along the Lower Assam river passes.

Event: Frontier Battle with Kamata Forces
Detailed Event Description: A pitched riverine engagement between Ahom war flotillas and Kamata defensive troops along the Lower Assam river passes.

Event: Military Stalemate in the Kamata Campaign
Detailed Event Description: After prolonged fighting and sieges without either side securing a decisive victory, both monarchs recognize mutual exhaustion.

Event: Military Stalemate in the Kamata Campaign

Event: Ahom-Kamata Royal Matrimonial Treaty
Detailed Event Description: Peace concluded by the marriage of Kamata Princess Rajani (Durlabhanarayana's daughter) to Sukhangphaa, sealing durable inter-kingdom peace.
Key Historical Figures: King Sukhangphaa, Princess Rajani, Raja Durlabhanarayana

Event: Birth of Prince Chao Pulai
Detailed Event Description: Princess Rajani gives birth to Prince Chao Pulai, tying the royal lineages of Kamata and Ahom together.
Key Historical Figures: King Sukhangphaa, Queen Rajani, Infant Chao Pulai

Event: Chao Pulai's Revolt and Alliance with Kamata
Detailed Event Description: Chao Pulai disputes the succession of his half-brother Sukhrangphaa and conspires with maternal Kamata envoys for military support.
Key Historical Figures: Prince Chao Pulai, King Sukhrangphaa, Kamata envoys

Event: Fraternal Reconciliation Between Sukhrangphaa and Chao Pulai
Detailed Event Description: Rather than shedding fraternal blood, Sukhrangphaa welcomes Chao Pulai back into the court and effects complete reconciliation.

Event: Appointment of Chao Pulai as Governor of Sadiya
Detailed Event Description: King Sukhrangphaa invests Chao Pulai with governorship of the critical eastern frontier outpost of Sadiya.

Event: Safrai River Diplomatic Peace Summit
Detailed Event Description: King Sutuphaa meets the Chutia monarch on the Safrai river for joint festivities and peace negotiations to resolve frontier friction.

Event: Betrayal and Assassination of King Sutuphaa
Detailed Event Description: During a boat excursion on the Safrai river, the Chutia king treacherously assassinates Sutuphaa aboard the barge, triggering centuries of bitter warfare.

Event: First Ministerial Interregnum
Detailed Event Description: Following Sutuphaa's treacherous assassination, the Burhagohain and Borgohain rule jointly for four years due to the absence of an acceptable adult royal prince.

Event: Banishment of the Pregnant Younger Queen
Detailed Event Description: While King Tyao Khamti is away battling Chutias, his jealous Chief Queen falsely accuses the beloved younger queen and sentences her to be cast adrift on a raft down the Brahmaputra.
Key Historical Figures: King Tyao Khamti, Chief Queen, Younger Queen (Mother of Sudangphaa)

Event: Birth of Prince Sudang in Habung Village
Detailed Event Description: The banished pregnant queen washes ashore at Habung and is sheltered by a pious Brahmin family; she gives birth to prince Sudang before passing away.
Key Historical Figures: Younger Queen, Brahmin of Habung, Infant Prince Sudang

Event: Assassination of King Tyao Khamti
Detailed Event Description: Disgusted by Tyao Khamti's acquiescence in the murder of his innocent queen and arbitrary rule, nobles and citizens revolt and assassinate the king.
Key Historical Figures: King Tyao Khamti, Ahom Nobles and Ministers

Event: Second Ministerial Interregnum
Detailed Event Description: Ministers Burhagohain and Borgohain hold executive power for eight years following the assassination of Tyao Khamti while searching for the exiled royal prince.

Event: Prince Sudang Raised in Brahmin Household
Detailed Event Description: Prince Sudang grows up oblivious to his royal identity, tending cattle and studying Sanskrit scriptures alongside Brahmin children at Habung.

Event: Sudangphaa Identity Confirmation
Detailed Event Description: Official confirmation of royal bloodline presented to Prince Sudang at Habung by council messengers.

Event: Ministers Discover the Hidden Prince Sudang at Habung
Detailed Event Description: After eight years of search, the Burhagohain's emissaries locate the rightful heir Prince Sudang living as an ordinary cowherd at Habung.
Key Historical Figures: Prince Sudang, Royal Emissaries, Habung Brahmin

Event: Triumphant Royal Return of Sudang to Charaideo
Detailed Event Description: Prince Sudang is escorted in state barge flotillas up the Brahmaputra to Charaideo accompanied by his Brahmin foster-family.
Key Historical Figures: Prince Sudang, Brahmin foster family, Gohains

Event: Coronation of Sudangphaa
Detailed Event Description: Grand accession ceremony where Prince Sudang ascends the throne taking the Tai title Chao Siu-Dang-Pha.

Event: The Reign of Bamuni Konwar
Detailed Event Description: Sudangphaa rewards his Brahmin foster father and brothers with high court offices, inaugurating Hindu Brahminical influence.

Event: Institution of the Singari-Gharutha Coronation
Detailed Event Description: Sudangphaa inaugurates the sacred Singari-gharutha ceremony, ascending a raised platform of Singari timber, washing in sacred waters, and killing a bull/buffalo.

Event: Harmonious Synthesis of Tai and Hindu Vedic Rituals
Detailed Event Description: Court ceremonies conduct Vedic homa rituals alongside traditional Tai worship of Somdeo and Me-Dam-Me-Phi ancestor rites.
Key Historical Figures: King Sudangphaa, Hindu Brahmins, Tai Deodhais

Event: Harmonious Synthesis of Tai and Hindu Vedic Rituals
Detailed Event Description: Court ceremonies conduct Vedic homa rituals alongside traditional Tai worship of Somdeo and Me-Dam-Me-Phi ancestor rites.
Key Historical Figures: King Sudangphaa, Hindu Brahmins, Tai Deodhais

Event: Matrimonial Alliance with Bhuyan Chieftains
Detailed Event Description: Sudangphaa secures stability across the north bank by establishing marriage ties with powerful Baro-Bhuyan chieftains.

Event: Administrative Centralization at Charagua
Detailed Event Description: Constructs the new capital city Charagua on the Dihing river to better oversee burgeoning agricultural lands and trade routes.

Event: Cultural Renaissance and Literary Patronage
Detailed Event Description: Sudangphaa patronizes both Tai chroniclers and Sanskrit scholars, fostering bilingualism and literary learning in court.

Event: Peaceful Reign of Sujanphaa
Detailed Event Description: Sujanphaa preserves external peace and internal order across Upper Assam for fifteen unbroken years.

Event: Consolidation Under Suphakphaa
Detailed Event Description: Son of Sujanphaa; a steady seventeen-year reign promoting trade, agricultural stability, and peace with neighboring hill tribes.

Event: The Golden Forty-Nine-Year Peace of Susenphaa
Detailed Event Description: One of the longest reigns in Ahom annals; nearly five decades of uninterrupted agricultural and population growth.

Event: Tangshu Naga Raids on Lowland Settlements
Detailed Event Description: Tangshu Naga warriors raid eastern border villages, looting grain stores and capturing lowland subjects.

Event: Susenphaa's Punitive Tangshu Campaign
Detailed Event Description: Susenphaa personally leads an army into the rugged Tangshu hills, encircling rebel villages and cutting off mountain passes.

Event: Submission and Tribute of the Tangshu Chiefs
Detailed Event Description: Defeated Tangshu leaders present offerings of swords, amber, and mountain goods, swearing eternal peace with the Ahom throne.

Event: Erection of Charaideo Boundary Stones
Detailed Event Description: Inscribed stone monoliths erected around the holy hills of Charaideo to permanently safeguard the royal necropolis.

Event: The Battle of Turung Against the Kacharis
Detailed Event Description: Ahom forces clash fiercely with Kachari armies near the Dikhou; Ahom army suffers a tactical reverse leading to temporary tribute concessions.
Key Historical Figures: King Suhenphaa, Kachari King, Borgohain Khenphung

Event: Peace Settlement with the Kacharis
Detailed Event Description: Suhenphaa concludes peace with the Kachari king through tribute of royal princesses and elephants, stabilizing the southern flank.

Event: Tangshu Ambush of Borgohain Khenphung
Detailed Event Description: During a patrol in the eastern hill tracts, Borgohain Khenphung is ambushed by hostile Tangshu warriors but manages a fighting retreat.

Event: Suhenphaa's Inspection of Palace Works
Detailed Event Description: King Suhenphaa walks unescorted among workmen to inspect new wooden palace structures at Charagua.

Event: Assassination of King Suhenphaa
Detailed Event Description: Turung palace laborers conceal weapons and spear King Suhenphaa to death inside the palace under cover of darkness.

Event: Assassination of King Suhenphaa

Event: Royal Inquest and Execution of Suhenphaa's Assassins
Detailed Event Description: Supimphaa convenes a tribunal, identifies the conspirators behind his father's murder, and executes them publicly.

Event: Supimphaa Exiles Pregnant Queen to the Nagas
Detailed Event Description: Due to malicious palace gossip, Supimphaa banishes his pregnant queen to the village of a loyal Naga chief.
Key Historical Figures: King Supimphaa, Exiled Queen, Naga Chief

Event: Birth of Konseng in the Naga Foothills
Detailed Event Description: The exiled queen gives birth to prince Konseng among the Nagas, raised in mountain traditions before returning to court.
Key Historical Figures: Infant Konseng, Exiled Queen, Naga foster family

Event: Konseng's Return and Presentation to King Suhungmung
Detailed Event Description: Grown into a stalwart warrior, Konseng is brought from the Naga village to Bakata; Suhungmung acknowledges him as half-brother of royal blood.

Event: Creation of the Office of Barpatragohain
Detailed Event Description: Suhungmung creates a third great ministerial post—the Barpatragohain—elevating Konseng to equal rank with Burhagohain and Borgohain.

Event: Adoption of the Title Swarganarayan and Saka Calendar
Detailed Event Description: Suhungmung officially assumes the Sanskrit title 'Swarganarayan' (Lord of Heaven), introducing the Saka calendar into state epigraphy.

Event: Ahom Vanguard Marches Against the Chutia Kingdom
Detailed Event Description: Suhungmung marches an immense land and naval force up the Brahmaputra to confront Chutia monarch Dhirnarayan.
Key Historical Figures: King Suhungmung, Ahom commanders, Chutia garrison

Event: Annexation of the Chutia Kingdom
Detailed Event Description: Chutia forces routed at Chandangiri; Sadiya annexed into the Ahom Empire; office of Sadiya-Khowa Gohain instituted; firearms and copper-plate treasures acquired.
Key Historical Figures: King Suhungmung, Dhirnarayan, First Sadiyakhowa Gohain

Event: Konseng Fortifies the Western Border
Detailed Event Description: Konseng Barpatragohain deploys stockades, signal towers, and cannon batteries along the western border to counter Bengal Sultanate raids.

Event: Repulse of Early Bengal Sultanate Invasions
Detailed Event Description: Ahom armies defeat Bengal Sultanate commanders Bit Malik and Mit Manik in naval battles, capturing artillery and cavalry horses.
Key Historical Figures: King Suhungmung, Konseng Barpatragohain, Bit Malik

Event: The Great Invasion of Commander Turbak
Detailed Event Description: General Turbak invades Assam with a large Gaur army armed with muskets, heavy cannons, and cavalry.
Key Historical Figures: General Turbak, King Suhungmung, Konseng Barpatragohain

Event: Decisive Victory Over Turbak and Pursuit to Karatoya
Detailed Event Description: Konseng Barpatragohain slays Turbak on the battlefield; Bengal forces routed; Ahoms pursue retreating invaders to the sacred Karatoya River.

Event: Foreign Captives Brought Before the Ahom Golden Throne
Detailed Event Description: Captured enemy generals, cavalry officers, and spoils of war presented before the Swarganarayan in solemn assembly.

Event: Ahom Naval Flotilla River Engagement
Detailed Event Description: Ahom Bachari war-boats and rowers maneuver against enemy rivercraft with bowmen and bow mounted swivel-guns.
Key Historical Figures: Ahom naval warriors, War boat helmsmen

Event: Strategic War Council in the Royal Chamber
Detailed Event Description: The king and top commanders review maps, troop movements, river currents, and fortress fortifications on the eve of battle.

Event: The Swarganarayan Invests the Royal Commander
Detailed Event Description: The monarch presents the consecrated Hengdang (royal curved sword) and battle garments to the appointed general.

Event: Ahom Commander Kneels in Fealty Before the King
Detailed Event Description: A royal commander kneels before the Ahom throne pledging absolute victory or martyrdom for the homeland.

Event: Accession of Suklenmung
Detailed Event Description: Suklenmung ascends the throne following Suhungmung's death, establishing Garhgaon as the royal residence.

Event: Construction of Fortified Capital Garhgaon and Naga Ali
Detailed Event Description: Excavates the monumental Garhgaon moat and earthen ramparts, builds brick gateways, and constructs the great Naga Ali military road.

Event: Battle of Pichala Against Koch Forces
Detailed Event Description: Suklenmung defends his kingdom against invading Koch commander Chilarai along the Pichala River, repulsing Koch forces with heavy losses.

Event: Solemn Celebration of the Rikkhvan Ceremony
Detailed Event Description: Performance of the ancient Tai Rikkhvan ritual to restore royal vitality, longevity, and invincibility in battle.
Key Historical Figures: King Suklenmung, Deodhai and Bailung high priests

Event: Royal Procession of King Sukhaamphaa
Detailed Event Description: Magnificent procession of Sukhaamphaa riding atop the royal tusker through Garhgaon with gold-embroidered silk standards.

Event: Royal Procession of King Sukhaamphaa
Detailed Event Description: Magnificent procession of Sukhaamphaa riding atop the royal tusker through Garhgaon with gold-embroidered silk standards.

Event: Chilarai's Invasion of Garhgaon
Detailed Event Description: Koch king Naranarayan and general Chilarai launch a blitzkrieg; Ahoms execute a tactical retreat into the hills of Namrup.
Key Historical Figures: King Sukhaamphaa, General Chilarai, King Naranarayan

Event: The Treaty of Majuli
Detailed Event Description: Peace treaty negotiated on Majuli island; Ahoms cede north bank lands and send royal hostages, enabling subsequent reclamation after Koch departure.
Key Historical Figures: King Sukhaamphaa, General Chilarai, Royal hostages

Event: The Long Peace and Cultural Growth Under Khora Raja
Detailed Event Description: Following early wars, Sukhaamphaa's kingdom experiences prolonged domestic peace, flourishing commerce, and arts.

Event: Accession of Susenghphaa (Pratap Singha)
Detailed Event Description: Pratap Singha ascends the throne at Garhgaon, inaugurating decades of revolutionary governance and resistance against the Mughal Empire.

Event: Accession of Susenghphaa (Pratap Singha)

Event: Reorganization of the Paik System by Momai Tamuli Barbarua
Detailed Event Description: Momai Tamuli reorganizes adult males into Paik squads (Gots of 3 or 4 men), mandatory rotation of state labor, and khel guilds, transforming Assam's agrarian and military mobilization.
Key Historical Figures: Momai Tamuli Barbarua, King Pratap Singha

Event: Institution of the Offices of Borbarua and Borphukan
Detailed Event Description: Pratap Singha creates two supreme executive posts: the Borbarua (prime administrator & chief judicial magistrate) and Borphukan (viceroy & supreme military warden of Lower Assam).
Key Historical Figures: King Pratap Singha, First Borbarua Momai Tamuli, First Borphukan Langi Panisiya

Event: Treaty of Asurar Ali and Western Defense Line
Detailed Event Description: Following repeated repulses of Mughal invasions, Pratap Singha signs the Treaty of Asurar Ali (1639) with Allah Yar Khan, formalizing the Barnadi River as the frontier.
Key Historical Figures: King Pratap Singha, Mughal General Allah Yar Khan, Momai Tamuli

Event: Tyranny and Court Intrigue Under Suramphaa
Detailed Event Description: Suramphaa becomes infatuated with a concubine, disregarding ministers and executing loyal nobles arbitrarily.
Key Historical Figures: King Suramphaa, Royal concubine, Ahom ministers

Event: Deposition and Poisoning of Suramphaa
Detailed Event Description: The council of ministers deposes the tyrannical king and removes him from power.

Event: The Frail Reign of Sutingphaa
Detailed Event Description: Afflicted by chronic disease and goitre, Sutingphaa struggles to rule while court factions vie for supremacy.

Event: Prince Sutamla Organizes Court Loyalists
Detailed Event Description: Prince Sutamla rallies ministers and soldiers to remove his incapacitated father to restore imperial governance.

Event: Coronation of Jayadhwaj Singha
Detailed Event Description: Sutamla ascends the throne taking the regal Hindu name Jayadhwaj Singha, the first Ahom monarch to issue coins with Sanskrit inscriptions.

Event: Solemn Vigil at the Royal Deathbed
Detailed Event Description: Court ministers, priests, and queens maintain vigil around the royal bed chamber as a Swargadeo departs for the realm of ancestors.
Key Historical Figures: Dying Ahom King, High ministers, Deodhais

Event: Adoption of Hindu Rituals in Sutamla's Court
Detailed Event Description: Sutamla formalizes Hindu court rituals, patronizing Vaishnava monasteries and adopting Sanskrit titulature alongside Tai liturgy.

Event: Royal Initiation into Ekasarana Dharma
Detailed Event Description: Jayadhwaj takes spiritual initiation from Niranjan Bapu of Auniati Satra, formally adopting Mahapuruxiya Ekasarana Dharma as royal faith.
Key Historical Figures: King Jayadhwaj Singha, Niranjan Deva of Auniati Satra

Event: Royal Initiation into Ekasarana Dharma
Detailed Event Description: Jayadhwaj takes spiritual initiation from Niranjan Bapu of Auniati Satra, formally adopting Mahapuruxiya Ekasarana Dharma as royal faith.
Key Historical Figures: King Jayadhwaj Singha, Niranjan Deva of Auniati Satra

Event: Royal Naam-Prasanga and Satra Endowments
Detailed Event Description: The king participates in choral chanting (Naam-Prasanga) and donates extensive rent-free lands and paiks to the satras of Majuli.
Key Historical Figures: King Jayadhwaj Singha, Satradhikars, Vaishnava bhakats

Event: Mir Jumla's Imperial Mughal Invasion
Detailed Event Description: Aurangzeb's premier general and Viceroy of Bengal, Mir Jumla, advances up the Brahmaputra with 12,000 cavalry, 30,000 infantry, and 323 armed war boats.
Key Historical Figures: Mir Jumla, King Jayadhwaj Singha, Dilir Khan

Event: Mughal Capture of Capital Garhgaon
Detailed Event Description: Mir Jumla enters Garhgaon in victory; thousands of Ahom cannons, gold treasures, and grain reserves are captured by imperial Mughal forces.
Key Historical Figures: Mir Jumla, Mughal garrison, Chronicler Shihabuddin Talish

Event: The Monsoon Counter-War of Namrup
Detailed Event Description: From hills of Namrup, Jayadhwaj unleashes guerrilla warfare during torrential monsoons, severing Mughal supply lines and decimating Mir Jumla's trapped army with epidemic fever.
Key Historical Figures: King Jayadhwaj Singha, Ahom guerrilla fighters, Mir Jumla

Event: The Treaty of Ghilajharighat
Detailed Event Description: Severely ill Mir Jumla and exhausted Jayadhwaj sign treaty; Ahoms cede Western Assam, pay war indemnities of gold, silver, 90 elephants, and send princesses.
Key Historical Figures: King Jayadhwaj Singha, Mir Jumla, Dilir Khan

Event: Departure of Princess Ramani Gabharu to Delhi
Detailed Event Description: Six-year-old Princess Ramani Gabharu (daughter of Jayadhwaj) is tearfully handed over as part of the treaty to be sent to Delhi, where she later marries Prince Azam Shah as Rahmat Banu Begum.

Event: Departure of Princess Ramani Gabharu to Delhi

Key Historical Figures: Princess Ramani Gabharu, King Jayadhwaj Singha, Mughal officers

Event: King Jayadhwaj Singha's Vow of Liberation
Detailed Event Description: Brokenhearted by the humiliating treaty and daughter's departure, Jayadhwaj returns to ruined Garhgaon and urges the court never to rest until the Mughals are expelled.

Event: Deathbed of King Jayadhwaj Singha
Detailed Event Description: On his deathbed at Bakata, Jayadhwaj extracts a solemn oath from his successor Chakradhwaj Singha to wipe out the shame of Mughal conquest.
Key Historical Figures: King Jayadhwaj Singha, Prince Chakradhwaj Singha

Event: Chakradhwaj Singha's Oath of Resistance
Detailed Event Description: Receiving a patronizing Mughal royal robe (khilat) from Delhi, King Chakradhwaj angrily throws it down, proclaiming: 'Death is preferable to a state of subordination to the Bengas!'

Event: Lachit Tested and Appointed Supreme Commander
Detailed Event Description: Chakradhwaj tests Lachit's presence of mind with a staged court insult; impressed by his fierce dignity, the king confers the golden sword and supreme command of the army to liberate Guwahati.

Event: Lachit Borphukan Liberates Guwahati
Detailed Event Description: Ahom forces execute a coordinated amphibious night assault, breaching the Mughal ramparts and driving imperial troops out of Guwahati.
Key Historical Figures: Lachit Borphukan, Mughal commander Firuz Khan
